The 'expr' attribute is used to define the expression used by jit.expr to calculate the output.
multiply left inlet and right inlet
outputs the left inlet with no change
prefix C74:/media/jitter/, insert 0 Browse..., insert 1 <separator>, symbol $1
Non-input expressions will cache the calculation by default, for efficiency.  For operations like jit.noise, you might want to turn off 'cache'
prefix C74:/media/jitter/, insert 0 Browse..., insert 1 <separator>, symbol $1
You can also use jit.bfg functions and many Jitter MOP objects within an expression

Also supports these mathematically useful constants:
PI, TWOPI, HALFPI, INVPI, DEGTORAD, RADTODEG, E, LN2, LN10, LOG10E, LOG2E, SQRT2, SQRT1_2

These variables can be used in an expression.  The number between the brackets defines the index.  For example 'in[0]' is the first input, 'in[1]' the second input.  Similarly 'norm[0]' generates normalized values across the first dimension (horizontal) and 'norm[1]' across the second (vertical).
